forcedChoices.choice: «Dios es todo y está en todo»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces ser/estar; 'is all' is identity (ser), 'in all' is location (estar).
'becomes actual' in the potential/actual sense; glossary form 'en acto'.

forcedChoices.choice: «se adhieran y se sostengan en él» (also 3:5.4 «se sostienen»)
forcedChoices.reason: 'consist' in the older sense of hold together, not 'consist of'.
The English capitalizes 'Himself' here only; the capital is kept.
'ajustarse con' keeps both readings (adapts to / works together with) and the link to 'Ajustadores'.
A bare 'su' could be read as God's viewpoint; the plural 'ustedes' marks the reader.

forcedChoices.choice: «él conoce la hechura de ustedes; recuerda que son polvo»
forcedChoices.reason: 'you' addressed to every human being; plural 'ustedes' per the variety rules.

forcedChoices.choice: «que él puede enviar y que puede llegar a enviar»
forcedChoices.reason: 'can and may' keeps capacity and possibility without choosing permission.
Agree with 'las criaturas de Havona'; no claim about sex.
Spanish has no exact pair for brave/courageous; distinct words keep the contrast in 3:5.17.
«altruismo» is used for 'altruism' in 3:5.7; a different word keeps the two items apart.
Spanish needs a gender; the masculine generic matches the English general sense of 'child'.
The English states a condition of the world; the indicative keeps it a statement.
'su' keeps open whether 'their' refers to the streams, the life, or the mind.
